Project Purpose
This is a Blueprint Document / BRD generation system. Its business goal is to help consultants or business analysts
create structured solution blueprint documents faster by combining:
●​
user-provided project documents,
●​
reusable repositories of reference documents,
●​
web research,
●​
OpenAI-generated section content,
●​
editable templates,
●​
DOCX/TXT export.
In plain terms: a user creates a client project, uploads documents, configures/generates sections, approves the output,
and exports a polished Blueprint Docume

10.​ User may import/apply a DOCX template.
11.​ User opens the editor.
12.​ User reviews section structure, keywords, sources, and generated content.
13.​ Backend uses uploaded chunks, optional web search, OpenAI, and image metadata to generate section
content.
14.​ User approves generated sections.
15.​ User exports the final Blueprint Document as DOCX/TXT.
16.​ Project or repository can be exported/imported as ZIP.

Morning:
●​
Run the app locally.
●​
Create one test project.
●​
Upload one small DOCX or TXT.
●​
Watch /api/projects/{id}/files change from uploaded to indexed.
●​
Read project_routes.py and chunking_pipeline.py.
Afternoon:
●​
Open /editor?project_id=<id>.
●​
Generate one section.
●​
Read screen3_routes.py around section generation/export.
●​
Export a DOCX and inspect how brd_workflow.py formats it.
End of day:
●​
Trace one complete request from button click in screen3.html to FastAPI route to OpenAI call to
JSON/DOCX output.
●​
Review .env variables.
●​
Note the stale/mismatched parts: React

Database And Storage
There is no external database server.
Storage is local:
●​
SQLite: app/users.db for users
●​
JSON files: project state, repository state, templates, section config
●​
uploaded files: app/uploads
●​
generated chunks: chunks.json
●​
extracted images: app/extracted_images
●​
image metadata: app/image_chunks.json
●​
exports: outputs, output, and app/static/exports
Example: when a PDF is uploaded, it is saved under a project folder, chunked into text records, and those chunks are
stored in JSON.
APIs
Major API groups:
●​
Auth: POST /signup, POST /login, GET /approve/{token}
●​

APP_BASE_URL=http://localhost:8010
How To Run Locally
From repo root:
cd c:\22-05_BDGAgent\19-05_BDGAgent\orchestration\brd_convo_app\backend
python -m venv venv
venv\Scripts\activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8010 --reload
Then open:
http://localhost:8010
If using the separate web tools service, from repo root:
cd c:\22-05_BDGAgent\19-05_BDGAgent
uvicorn infrastructure.mcp_web_tools.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000
Beginner Onboarding Guide
Start with this mental model:
Projects hold client work.
Uploads become chunks.
Chunks become sear

Frontend
The frontend is not a separate React app in the current tree. The README mentions React, but the actual visible
app is static HTML served from:
app/static
Key pages:
●​
index.html: login/signup and legacy chat UI
●​
projects.html: project list/create/delete
●​
document-upload.html: upload source/prompt docs
●​
screen3.html: Blueprint Document editor/generator
●​
repositories.html: reusable document repositories
●​
templates.html: template library
●​
image_repo.html: image repository UI
●​
help.html: user guide page
Backend
The backend is a FastAPI app. It registers routers for:
●​
pro

|
v
Optional MCP/Web Tools Services
|-- web_search
|-- open_url
|-- doc_search
|-- Serper/OpenAI search
Main Entry Points
Primary backend entry point:
app/main.py
Run target:
uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8010 --reload
Main browser entry point:
http://localhost:8010/
This serves:
static/index.html
There is also an MCP web tools FastAPI app here:
infrastructure/mcp_web_tools/app/main.py
Important Note
The repo contains older conversational-agent code in conversation.py, and the login page calls /chat, but I did not
find a registered /chat route in app.main. The currently wired prod
